intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Stickler syndrome type VI (STL6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene (120270) on chromosome 20q13.33.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI (STL6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the second case of autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for a loss of function mutation in COL9A3, which encodes the α3 chain of type IX procollagen.
checks.explanation: The paper states that homozygous COL9A3 loss-of-function mutation causes autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. The STL6 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The COL9A3 gene is located on chromosome 20q13.33.
checks.evidence_quote: loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosome location, but adding a gene's standard location to a gene the paper names counts as supported nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder. Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that its main features are eye involvement, especially high myopia, and sensorineural hearing loss, sometimes with skeletal findings. As Faletra et al. (2014) noted, it is one of the recessive forms of Stickler syndrome caused by defects in type IX collagen.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the second case of autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for a loss of function mutation in COL9A3
checks.explanation: The paper describes the COL9A3 form as autosomal recessive, and the introduction calls Stickler syndrome a connective tissue disorder.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that the main features of Stickler syndrome type VI are eye involvement, especially high myopia, and sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: All of the Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects have exhibited high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild–severe hearing loss.
checks.explanation: The paper names high myopia and hearing loss as consistent features, and the abstract specifies the hearing loss as sensorineural.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that Stickler syndrome type VI sometimes includes skeletal findings.
checks.evidence_quote: including moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss, high myopia, and both tibial and femoral bowing at birth. Radiographs demonstrated abnormal capital femoral epiphyses and mild irregularities of the vertebral endplates.
checks.explanation: The paper reports skeletal findings in the COL9A3 cases.

checks.claim: Faletra et al. (2014) noted that Stickler syndrome type VI is one of the recessive forms of Stickler syndrome caused by defects in type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: recessive forms have been associated with mutations of COL9A1 (OMIM 120210) and COL9A2 (OMIM 120260) genes. Type IX collagen is a heterotrimeric molecule formed by three genetically distinct chains: α1, α2, and α3 encoded by the COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 genes.
checks.explanation: The abstract links recessive Stickler syndrome to the type IX collagen genes, and this paper adds COL9A3 to them.

paragraphs.text: Faletra et al. (2014) described a family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.

checks.claim: Faletra et al. (2014) described a family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) described a single proband with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. His only sib, a sister, was unaffected. He had myopia and moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) described a single male proband with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient failed his newborn hearing screen.
checks.explanation: The paper describes one male proband (the text uses 'his') with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.

checks.claim: The only sib of the Stickler syndrome proband reported by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) was a sister who was unaffected.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient has one older sister. There is no report of hearing loss, myopia, other ocular anomalies, or skeletal anomalies in either parent or in the sister.
checks.explanation: The paper states the proband has one sister and reports no features in her; elsewhere she is called an unaffected sibling.

checks.claim: The Stickler syndrome proband reported by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) had myopia.
checks.evidence_quote: by 2 years, he had developed myopia of −6.75 OD and −8 OS. By 12 years, this had progressed to −10.75 OD and −11.25 OS.
checks.explanation: The paper documents the proband's myopia and its progression.

checks.claim: The Stickler syndrome proband reported by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) had moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: The features of the patient described here were similar, including moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss, high myopia
checks.explanation: The paper reports moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss in the proband.

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) showed that Stickler syndrome type VI is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, based on the families reported by Faletra et al. (2014) and Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018).

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) showed that Stickler syndrome type VI is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, based on the families reported by Faletra et al. (2014) and Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018).
checks.evidence_quote: As in the case described here, the three siblings with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome described by were homozygous for a loss-of-function mutation in COL9A3.
checks.explanation: The paper reports the second family with homozygous mutations and heterozygous carrier parents, and compares it with the earlier family, so recessive inheritance is supported. Saying the paper 'showed' this from both families claims more than the paper itself does.

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that other autosomal recessive forms of Stickler syndrome are caused by mutations in the COL9A1 gene (Stickler syndrome type IV) and in the COL9A2 gene (Stickler syndrome type V).

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that an autosomal recessive form of Stickler syndrome, Stickler syndrome type IV, is caused by mutations in the COL9A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Five families have been described with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in the COL9A1 and COL9A2 type IX procollagen genes
checks.explanation: The paper states that COL9A1 mutations cause autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. The 'type IV' label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that an autosomal recessive form of Stickler syndrome, Stickler syndrome type V, is caused by mutations in the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Five families have been described with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in the COL9A1 and COL9A2 type IX procollagen genes
checks.explanation: The paper states that COL9A2 mutations cause autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. The 'type V' label is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: In a family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Faletra et al. (2014) found a loss-of-function mutation in the COL9A3 gene.

checks.claim: In a family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Faletra et al. (2014) found a loss-of-function mutation in the COL9A3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family due to loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene.

paragraphs.text: In a single proband with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) found a homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene. His parents and his unaffected sib were all heterozygous for the mutation.

checks.claim: In a single male proband with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) found a homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: exome sequencing was used to identify homozygosity for single base duplication c.650dupC in exon 13 of COL9A3 (RefSeq accession number NM_001853.3) of the proband.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous COL9A3 mutation in the male proband.

checks.claim: The parents of the Stickler syndrome proband reported by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) were heterozygous for the COL9A3 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Genotyping of the parents and an unaffected sibling showed that all of them were heterozygous for the sequence change
checks.explanation: The paper states the parents were heterozygous.

checks.claim: The unaffected sib of the Stickler syndrome proband reported by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) was heterozygous for the COL9A3 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Genotyping of the parents and an unaffected sibling showed that all of them were heterozygous for the sequence change
checks.explanation: The paper states the unaffected sibling was heterozygous.
